chapter: Maynard Ferguson and the drinking life
title: Drugs and drinking and how they affect playing
summary: He compares pot, cocaine and alcohol and how booze makes him play looser.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: The whole band, the Glenn Miller band is over. So nobody dared like even —

Right. There was some peer pressure there. Yeah, wow, I’ve heard of some stories but I never heard that kind of story. Do you think you play differently if you’re under the influence than if you’re not?

Influence of what? I play differently when I’m drinking than when I’m not drinking. But pot, I’ve lost interest. I mean I smoked so much pot it was unbelievable. But I’m not so interested in that anymore. That paranoia feeling has kind of left me. Marching powder — Peruvian marching powder, also known as cocaine — that makes you rush, so I try to stay off of that unless I really need a lift. But that’s just the way all of that stuff went down.
But does booze make you play —
It makes me take more chances and it makes me play looser.
Looser. Okay. And you find that, at least at that time, was it similar for your bandmates too?
